'''George Frederick Blanda''' (September 17, 1927 – September 27, 2010) was an American professional [[American football|football]] [[quarterback]] and [[placekicker]] who played in the [[American Football League]] (AFL) and [[National Football League]] (NFL). Blanda played 26 seasons of professional football, the most in the sport's history, and had scored more points than anyone in history at the time of his retirement.

Blanda retired from professional football in August 1976 as the sport's oldest player at the age of 48, a mark that still stands.<ref name=ctooldgn>{{cite news |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=ynRhAAAAIBAJ&sjid=nO0DAAAAIBAJ&pg=5480%2C4128090 |work=Spokesman-Review |location=Spokane, Washington |agency=Associated Press |title=Blanda called too old again |date=August 26, 1976 |page=43}}</ref><ref name=pullfoos>{{cite news |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=dCFOAAAAIBAJ&sjid=q-0DAAAAIBAJ&pg=3189%2C3082609 |work=Spokesman-Review |location=Spokane, Washington |agency=Associated Press |title=George Blanda not bitter, pulls for Oakland success |date=December 23, 1976 |page=23}}</ref> One of only three players to play in four different decades (the other two being [[John Carney (American football)|John Carney]] and [[Jeff Feagles]]), he holds the record for most extra points made (943) and attempted (959).<ref name=NYT-20100927>{{cite news | url=https://www.nytimes.com/2010/09/28/sports/football/28blanda.html | date=September 27, 2010 | access-date=September 28, 2010 | newspaper=The New York Times | title=George Blanda, Hall of Fame Football Player, Dies at 83 | author1=Frank Litsky | author2=Bruce Weber}}</ref>

'''Eugene Thurman Upshaw Jr.''' (August 15, 1945 – August 20, 2008) was an American professional [[American football|football]] [[guard (gridiron football)|guard]] who played for the [[Oakland Raiders]] of the [[American Football League]] (AFL) and later the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He later served as the executive director of the [[National Football League Players Association]] (NFLPA). Upshaw was inducted into the [[Pro Football Hall of Fame]] in 1987 and is also the only player in NFL history to reach the [[Super Bowl]] with the same team in three different decades.

'''Gary Wayne Zimmerman''' (born December 13, 1961) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Pro Football Hall of Fame|Hall of Fame]] [[Tackle (gridiron football position)|offensive tackle]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) and [[United States Football League]] (USFL). He earned a [[Super Bowl ring]] with the [[Denver Broncos]] ([[Super Bowl XXXII]]).

Zimmerman was born in [[Fullerton, California]] and played scholastically at [[Walnut High School]] in the [[San Gabriel Valley]] of [[California]].<ref name="PFR1">{{Cite web |title=Gary Zimmerman Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/Z/ZimmGa00.htm |access-date=2025-07-13 |website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]] |language=en}}</ref> He played collegiately at [[Oregon Ducks football|Oregon]], and was a first-team [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] as a senior.<ref name="NFL">{{cite web |url=https://www.nfl.com/players/gary-zimmerman/ |title=Gary Zimmerman Stats |website=NFL.com |access-date=May 11, 2024}}</ref><ref name=NEA>{{cite news|title=The 1983 NEA All-America team|newspaper=The Republic (Columbus, Ind.)|date=November 30, 1983|page=16|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/4574799/1983_nea_allamerica_team/|via=Newspapers.com}} {{Open access}}</ref> He was inducted into the [[Oregon Sports Hall of Fame]] in 2002.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.oregonsportshall.org/gary_zimmerman.html |title=Oregon Sports Hall of Fame |access-date=May 4, 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120513190828/http://oregonsportshall.org/gary_zimmerman.html |archive-date=May 13, 2012 }}</ref>

Zimmerman played for the [[Minnesota Vikings]] from 1986 to 1992 and for the [[Denver Broncos]] from 1993 to 1997.<ref name="nfl.com">{{Cite web|url=http://www.nfl.com/player/garyzimmerman/2503860/profile|title = Gary Zimmerman Stats, News and Video - T|website = [[NFL.com]]}}</ref> He won [[Super Bowl XXXII]] with the Broncos against the [[1997 Green Bay Packers season|Green Bay Packers]]. He was selected to the [[Pro Bowl]] seven times and was an All-Pro selection eight times. He was inducted into the [[Pro Football Hall of Fame]] in 2008.

'''Gene Vincent Mruczkowski''' (born June 6, 1980) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Guard (American football)|guard]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Purdue Boilermakers football|Purdue Boilermakers]] and was signed by the [[New England Patriots]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2003. 

Mruczkowski, who also played for the [[Miami Dolphins]], earned [[Super Bowl ring]]s with the Patriots in [[Super Bowl XXXVIII]] and [[Super Bowl XXXIX]]. He is the older brother of NFL offensive lineman [[Scott Mruczkowski]]. Over the years, Mruczkowski has become a successful business owner.
